summary: Above all בְּרִית, covenant: a binding agreement made, or “cut”, between two parties, sworn and often sealed with blood, a sign or a meal, which each must keep. Men make it with one another as treaty, alliance, friendship or marriage; Yahweh makes it with Noah, with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, with Israel at Horeb, with Levi and with David, and promises a new and everlasting covenant, which Jesus made in his blood. The verb בָּרָה is to eat, of bread brought to the sick or the mourning, with its nouns בִּרְיָה and בָּרוּת “food”; scripture does not say whether בְּרִית comes from it, though covenants were sealed with a meal.

words.summary: About 285 times. A covenant is “cut” (כָּרַת), “established” (הֵקִים), “given”, “kept” and “remembered”, or “broken” (הֵפֵר) and “transgressed” (עָבַר); it stands “between me and you” (Gen 9:12; 17:2; 31:44), is sworn with an oath or curse (Gen 26:28; Deu 29:11), and has a sign (Gen 9:12; 17:11), blood (Exo 24:8), or a meal (Gen 26:30; 31:54; Exo 24:11). How the noun comes from the root is not clear: the verb of the root means eat, and covenants were sealed by eating together, but the text never links the two words; Akkadian birītu “fetter” and birīt “between” are other possible ties.

senses.gloss: covenant between men: treaty, alliance, pact
senses.definition: A sworn agreement between men, peoples or kings: a treaty of peace, an alliance in war, a pact of friendship, the terms on which a king rules or a city surrenders. Those bound by it are its בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית, “covenant partners, allies”.

evidence.note: Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and cattle, “and the two of them cut a בְּרִית.”
“Let there be an oath (אָלָה) between us, between us and you, and let us cut a בְּרִית with you”; a feast follows (Gen 26:30).
Laban to Jacob: “Let us cut a בְּרִית, I and you, and let it be a witness between me and you”; they ate there on the heap (Gen 31:46, 54).
Mamre, Eshcol and Aner “were בַּעֲלֵי בְרִית of Abram”: his allies, who went with him to war (Gen 14:24).
Solomon and Hiram: “there was peace between Hiram and Solomon, and the two of them cut a בְּרִית.”
Ahab lets Ben-hadad go “with a בְּרִית”: terms of surrender.
Joshua made peace with the Gibeonites and cut a covenant to let them live; the men had taken of their provisions and not asked Yahweh (Jos 9:14).
The men of Jabesh: “Cut a covenant with us and we will serve you.”
“Jonathan and David cut a בְּרִית, because he loved him as his own soul”: a covenant of friendship.
“You have brought your servant into a covenant of Yahweh with you.”
Abner to David: “Cut your covenant with me, and my hand will be with you.”
King David cut a covenant with the elders of Israel at Hebron before Yahweh, and they anointed him king.
Nebuchadnezzar took one of the royal seed “and cut a covenant with him and brought him into an oath”; breaking it is despising the oath (Ezk 17:18).
Tyre “did not remember the בְּרִית of brothers.”
“All the men of your covenant have sent you to the border”: allies who betrayed Edom.
The nations “cut a covenant” against Yahweh.

senses.definition: Marriage as a covenant, with God as witness: the wife is the “wife of your covenant”.

evidence.note: “Yahweh has been witness between you and the wife of your youth, with whom you have dealt treacherously, though she is your companion and אֵשֶׁת בְּרִיתֶךָ.”
The strange woman “forsakes the companion of her youth and forgets the בְּרִית of her God”.
Yahweh of Jerusalem: “I swore to you and entered into a covenant with you … and you became mine”.

senses.gloss: covenant (figurative): a binding resolve or settled peace
senses.definition: Said of a binding resolve, or of peace with what threatens: a covenant with one's eyes, with the stones of the field, with death and the grave.

evidence.note: “I cut a בְּרִית with my eyes; how then could I look upon a virgin?”
“You shall have a covenant with the stones of the field, and the beasts of the field shall be at peace with you.”
“We have cut a בְּרִית with death, and with the grave (שְׁאוֹל) we have made an agreement”; it will not stand (Isa 28:18).
Of Leviathan: “Will he cut a covenant with you, that you take him as a servant for ever?”

senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh makes, or “establishes”, with men: he binds himself by promise and oath, gives its terms and a sign, keeps it and remembers it; men keep it or break it. It is “my covenant”, “his covenant”, “the covenant of Yahweh”, “a holy covenant”.

evidence.note: “The faithful God, who keeps the בְּרִית and the חֶסֶד with those who love him and keep his commandments, to a thousand generations.”
“The counsel of Yahweh is with those who fear him, and his בְּרִית, to make them know it.”
“He will remember his covenant for ever.”
The king of the north's “heart shall be against the holy covenant (בְּרִית קֹדֶשׁ)”; also Dan 11:30, 32.
“Those who act wickedly against the covenant he will corrupt with flatteries, but the people who know their God shall be strong and act.”
To the Israelites belong “the glory and the covenants (αἱ διαθῆκαι) and the giving of the law … and the promises”.
The Gentiles were “strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope and without God in the world”.

senses.gloss: the covenant with Noah and all flesh
senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh established with Noah, his seed and every living soul never again to destroy all flesh by a flood, with the bow in the cloud as its sign.

evidence.note: “I will establish my covenant with you, and you shall go into the ark.”
“I establish my covenant with you: all flesh shall not again be cut off by the waters of the flood.”
“This is the sign of the בְּרִית which I give between me and you and every living soul (נֶפֶשׁ חַיָּה) … for everlasting generations.”
“I will remember my covenant … and the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.”

senses.gloss: the covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob
senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh cut with Abraham and established with Isaac and Jacob: to be God to Abraham and his seed, to multiply him, and to give him and his seed the land of Canaan for ever; its sign was circumcision.

evidence.note: “On that day Yahweh cut a בְּרִית with Abram, saying, To your seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates.”
“I will establish my covenant between me and you and your seed after you … for an everlasting covenant, to be God to you and to your seed after you”; the land follows in Gen 17:8.
“I will give my covenant between me and you, and multiply you exceedingly.”
“This is my covenant which you shall keep … every male among you shall be circumcised”; it is “a sign of the covenant” (Gen 17:11) and “my covenant in your flesh” (Gen 17:13).
The uncircumcised male “has broken my covenant”.
“I will establish my covenant with him [Isaac] for an everlasting covenant for his seed after him.”
“God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac and with Jacob.”
“I established my covenant with them, to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings.”
“I will remember my covenant with Jacob … Isaac … Abraham, and the land I will remember.”
The covenant made with Abraham, sworn to Isaac, “an everlasting covenant to Israel, saying, To you I will give the land of Canaan”.
“You found his heart faithful before you, and cut with him the covenant to give the land of the Canaanite.”
Yahweh was gracious to Israel “because of his covenant with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob”.
“To remember his holy covenant (διαθήκης), the oath which he swore to Abraham our father.”
“You are the sons … of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham, And in your seed shall all the families of the earth be blessed.”
“He gave him the covenant of circumcision.”
“A covenant confirmed beforehand by God, the law, which came 430 years after, does not annul.”

senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh made with Israel at Horeb when he brought them out of Egypt: its terms the ten words written on the tablets and the book of the covenant, sealed with blood, binding Israel to obey and Yahweh to make them his own people. The sabbath and the showbread were “an everlasting covenant” within it.

evidence.note: “If you will indeed hear my voice and keep my בְּרִית, you shall be my treasure among all peoples.”
Moses read “the book of the covenant”, and the people said, “All that Yahweh has spoken we will do and obey.”
“Behold the blood of the בְּרִית which Yahweh has cut with you concerning all these words.”
“He wrote on the tablets the words of the בְּרִית, the ten words.”
“He declared to you his covenant which he commanded you to do, the ten words.”
“Yahweh our God cut a covenant with us in Horeb … with us, all of us here alive today.”
“The tablets of the covenant.”
“These are the words of the covenant … in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which he cut with them in Horeb.”
Israel shall keep the sabbath “for their generations, an everlasting covenant”.
The showbread set out every sabbath, “an everlasting covenant”.
The ark, “in which is the covenant of Yahweh, which he cut with our fathers when he brought them out of the land of Egypt”.
“The house of Israel and the house of Judah have broken my covenant which I cut with their fathers.”
“Not like the covenant which I cut with their fathers in the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt, which they broke.”
Achan's theft: Israel “transgressed my covenant which I commanded them”.
“They have transgressed my covenant and rebelled against my law.”
“Because they forsook the covenant of Yahweh … which he cut with them when he brought them out of Egypt.”
Exo 24:8 quoted: “This is the blood of the covenant which God commanded you.”
“In the reading of the old covenant the same veil remains.”
“These are two covenants: one from mount Sinai, bearing children for slavery.”

senses.gloss: the covenant with Levi: priesthood, salt
senses.definition: The covenant with Levi and with Phinehas, of life, peace and an everlasting priesthood; and “a covenant of salt”, a lasting covenant, of the priests' portion and of salt on every offering.

evidence.note: “Behold, I give him my covenant of peace; and it shall be to him and his seed after him a covenant of everlasting priesthood.”
“My covenant was with him, life and peace, and I gave them to him for fear, and he feared me.”
“You have corrupted the covenant of Levi.”
“They have defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.”
The covenant with “the Levites the priests, my ministers” as sure as that with David.
The priests' portion: “a covenant of salt for ever before Yahweh, to you and your seed with you.”
“You shall not let the salt of the covenant of your God be lacking from your grain offering.”

senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh cut and swore with David: to establish his seed for ever and build his throne to all generations, a son of his to reign on it.

evidence.note: “I have cut a בְּרִית with my chosen, I have sworn to David my servant: your seed I will establish for ever, and build your throne to all generations.”
David's last words: “he has made with me a בְּרִית עוֹלָם, ordered in all things and kept.”
“For ever I will keep my חֶסֶד for him, and my covenant shall stand firm with him.”
“My covenant I will not profane, nor alter what has gone out of my lips.”
“You have renounced the covenant of your servant; you have profaned his crown to the ground.”
“If your sons keep my covenant … their sons also shall sit on your throne for ever.”
“If you can break my covenant with the day and my covenant with the night … then also my covenant with David my servant may be broken, that he should not have a son reigning on his throne.”
“Yahweh God of Israel gave the kingdom over Israel to David for ever, to him and his sons, by a covenant of salt.”
Yahweh would not destroy the house of David “because of the covenant that he had cut with David”.

senses.definition: The covenant Yahweh promises to cut with the house of Israel and the house of Judah in the days to come: a new covenant, everlasting, of peace, with his law written on their heart and their sin forgiven, made in the blood of the Christ.

evidence.note: “Days are coming … when I will cut with the house of Israel and the house of Judah בְּרִית חֲדָשָׁה.”
“This is the covenant … I will put my law within them and write it on their heart, and I will be their God and they shall be my people.”
“I will cut with them an everlasting covenant, that I will not turn away from them.”
Israel and Judah ask the way to Zion: “join yourselves to Yahweh in an everlasting covenant that will not be forgotten.”
“I will remember my covenant with you in the days of your youth, and establish for you an everlasting covenant.”
“I will cut with them a covenant of peace.”

“I will cut with them a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant it shall be with them … and set my sanctuary in their midst for ever”: Israel gathered into their land under David my servant (Ezk 37:21–25).
“The mountains may depart … but my חֶסֶד shall not depart from you, nor my covenant of peace be removed.”
“I will cut with you an everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David.”
“This is my covenant with them: my spirit that is upon you and my words … shall not depart from your mouth”; quoted in Rom 11:27.
“I will cut an everlasting covenant with them.”
The servant: “I will give you as a covenant of the people (לִבְרִית עָם), a light of the nations.”
“I will give you as a covenant of the people, to raise up the land, to cause to inherit the desolate inheritances”; Paul quotes it (2Co 6:2).
“I will cut for them a covenant in that day with the beasts of the field … and break bow and sword and battle from the land.”
“Because of the blood of your covenant I have sent your prisoners out of the pit.”
“The messenger of the covenant, whom you delight in, behold, he comes.”
“He shall confirm a covenant for the many one week.”
“This cup is the new covenant (ἡ καινὴ διαθήκη) in my blood, which is poured out for you.”
“This is my blood of the covenant, poured out for many for the forgiveness of sins.”
Jer 31:31–34 quoted of the covenant Christ mediates.
“And this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins.”
“Ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the spirit.”

senses.definition: A covenant the king and people cut before Yahweh, binding themselves to seek him and keep his commandments, or to do what his law requires; they “enter into” it and “stand” in it.

evidence.note: Josiah “cut the covenant before Yahweh, to walk after Yahweh and keep his commandments … to perform the words of this covenant written in this book; and all the people stood in the covenant.”
“They entered into the covenant to seek Yahweh the God of their fathers with all their heart and with all their soul.”
Jehoiada cut the covenant between Yahweh and the king and the people, to be Yahweh's people.
“Joshua cut a covenant with the people that day, and set them a statute and judgement in Shechem.”
Hezekiah: “It is in my heart to cut a covenant with Yahweh the God of Israel.”
“Let us cut a covenant with our God to put away all the wives.”
The release of slaves: “you cut a covenant before me in the house called by my name”; breaking it brought death (Jer 34:18–20).

evidence.locator: Gen.17.7; Exo.24.8; 2Sa.23.5; Isa.55.3; Jer.31.31; Dan.9.27, בְּרִית → διαθήκη; διαθήκη renders בְּרִית ×253

evidence.note: “This cup is the new covenant in my blood”: the בְּרִית חֲדָשָׁה of Jer 31:31.
Jer 31:31 quoted: “I will accomplish with the house of Israel … a new διαθήκην.”
Exo 24:8 quoted: “the blood of the διαθήκης.”
“His holy διαθήκης”, the covenant with Abraham.
A man's διαθήκη once confirmed is not annulled; the promise to Abraham is not annulled by the law.
“Where there is a διαθήκη, the death of the one who made it must be brought in”: the Greek word's sense of a will, read of the covenant made over a death.
“The blood of the everlasting διαθήκης”, the בְּרִית עוֹלָם.
“The ark of his διαθήκης was seen in his temple.”

parallels.note: “Covenant and steadfast love”: Yahweh keeps both; his חֶסֶד and his covenant of peace do not depart.
“Oath, curse”: the oath that binds a covenant, and the curses written in it.
“Oath”: the covenant with Abraham and the oath to Isaac.
“Testimony”: the covenant and its testimonies, kept together.
“Law”: to transgress the covenant is to rebel against the law.
“Statute”: the covenant with Jacob “for a statute”.

phrases.gloss: cut a covenant, make a covenant
who keeps the covenant and the steadfast love
the ark of the covenant of Yahweh
a covenant of salt: a lasting covenant

words.gloss: eat; give to eat, feed; (once) choose
words.summary: Nine tokens, all but one in 2 Samuel and Lamentations: the eating of bread, by the sick Amnon from Tamar's hand and by David in mourning, where the people came to feed him. 2Sa 13:5–6 sets it beside אָכַל in the same words, “and I will eat from her hand”. The qal בְּרוּ “choose” of 1Sa 17:8 is filed here by its form; how it comes from the root's sense is not clear. Two tokens filed here by spelling (Dan 4:12, 20, Aramaic בָּרָא “the field”) belong to another root.

senses.definition: To eat bread or food, of the sick and the mourning, who will eat or will not.

evidence.note: Amnon: “Let Tamar my sister come and make two cakes before my eyes, וְאֶבְרֶה from her hand”; in Jonadab's words the verb is אָכַל, “and I will eat (וְאָכַלְתִּי) from her hand” (2Sa 13:5).
“Bring the food (הַבִּרְיָה) into the chamber, וְאֶבְרֶה from your hand.”
David fasting for the child: “he was not willing, and did not eat (בָרָא, spelled with א) bread with them”; the next verses use אָכַל (2Sa 12:20–21).

senses.definition: Once, in Goliath's challenge: choose a man. Filed here by its form, an imperative of a verb with final ה.

evidence.note: “Am I not the Philistine, and you servants of Saul? בְּרוּ־לָכֶם a man, and let him come down to me.”

senses.definition: To make another eat: to bring bread to the mourning or the sick.

evidence.note: After Abner's burial “all the people came לְהַבְרוֹת David bread while it was still day, but David swore … if I taste bread or anything before the sun goes down”.
“Let Tamar my sister come וְתַבְרֵנִי bread, and make the food (הַבִּרְיָה) before my eyes.”

senses.definition: Once, of the famine in the siege of Jerusalem: children became food for their mothers. The form לְבָרוֹת may be the infinitive or a noun “food”.

evidence.note: “The hands of compassionate women boiled their children; they were לְבָרוֹת to them in the breaking of the daughter of my people.”

senses.definition: Food made and brought to one who is sick: the cakes Tamar made before Amnon's eyes. Only in 2Sa 13.

evidence.note: “Pretend to be sick … let her give me bread to eat and make הַבִּרְיָה before my eyes.”
David sent to Tamar: “Go to the house of Amnon your brother and make him הַבִּרְיָה.”
“Bring הַבִּרְיָה into the chamber”: it is the cakes (הַלְּבִבוֹת) she had made.

senses.definition: Food, set beside drink for thirst: once, in the psalm of the righteous sufferer fulfilled in Christ.

evidence.note: “They put gall (רֹאשׁ) in בָרוּתִי, and for my thirst they gave me vinegar to drink.”
“They gave him wine mixed with gall to drink, and having tasted it he would not drink.”
“That the scripture might be fulfilled, he says, I thirst”; they put a sponge full of vinegar to his mouth.

cognates.note: A bond that holds fast, Neo-Assyrian and Middle Assyrian. If בְּרִית is from a root “bind”, this is its kin; the Hebrew verb of the root does not mean bind, and nothing in scripture's use of בְּרִית decides it.

evidence.note: “clasp; fetter”.

cognates.note: Scripture's covenant stands “between me and you” (Gen 9:12; 17:2, 7, 10; 31:44), and some take בְּרִית for a bond “between” two parties; the Hebrew for “between” is בֵּין, not this root, and the tie is argued, not shown.

evidence.note: “between; within”.
“alley; between; clasp; dividing baulk; middle part; space between”.

cognates.note: The same consonants b-r and a weak third letter, and the same field of food and want of it; Akkadian's word for eating is akālu, as Hebrew אָכַל. Hunger, not eating, so only possible.

evidence.note: “be hungry”.
“hungry; hungry person”.

cognates.gloss: his body returned to health after being altered by disease
cognates.note: Recovery from sickness, as the food Tamar made for the sick Amnon and the bread brought to the mourning David; Lane notes the ه may stand for ء (بَرِئَ “be free of disease”), which would put it with Hebrew ברא rather than this root.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 196, art. بره, بَرِهَ (n2401)
evidence.note: “His body returned to a healthy state, or his health of body returned to him … after having been altered by disease. [The ه is perhaps a substitute for ء: see بَرِئَ.]”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh cut a covenant with Abram, “to your seed I have given this land, from the river of Egypt to the great river, the river Euphrates” (Gen 15:18), and established it as a בְּרִית עוֹלָם, “to be God to you and to your seed after you”, giving “to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession”; its sign was circumcision, “my covenant in your flesh” (Gen 17:7–8, 10–13). He established it with Isaac and Jacob, “to give them the land of Canaan, the land of their sojournings” (Exo 6:4; Psa 105:8–11), and when Israel is scattered for its sin he will remember it: “my covenant with Jacob … Isaac … Abraham I will remember, and the land I will remember” (Lev 26:42). Abraham himself was given none of the land, “not even a foot's breadth” (Act 7:5); he lived in the land of promise as a foreigner, and the fathers “died in faith, not having received the promises”, that they without us should not be made perfect (Heb 11:9, 13, 39–40). Jesus said they will be seen “in the kingdom of God” (Luk 13:28). Paul says the promises were spoken “to Abraham and to his seed … who is Christ”, that the covenant confirmed beforehand by God cannot be annulled by the law that came 430 years after, and that those baptized into Christ “are Abraham's seed, heirs according to the promise” (Gal 3:16–17, 27–29); those outside him are “strangers from the covenants of the promise, having no hope” (Eph 2:12). Zechariah said the coming of the Christ was God remembering “his holy covenant, the oath which he swore to Abraham” (Luk 1:72–73). From the verses: the covenant with Abraham promises the land of Canaan to Abraham and to his seed for ever; it has not yet been kept to Abraham, who died without it, and will be when Christ, the seed, comes and Abraham and the faithful are raised to inherit it in the kingdom of God; those baptized into Christ are heirs of the same covenant.

At Sinai Yahweh offered a covenant with a condition: “if you will indeed hear my voice and keep my covenant, you shall be my treasure among all peoples” (Exo 19:5). The people answered, “all that Yahweh has spoken we will do”, and Moses sprinkled them with “the blood of the covenant which Yahweh has cut with you” (Exo 24:7–8); its terms were the ten words written on the tablets of the covenant (Exo 34:28; Deu 4:13). Israel broke it: “they broke my covenant, though I was a husband to them” (Jer 31:32; 11:10), and the curses written in it came on them (Jer 11:8; Deu 29:20, 24). Jeremiah promised a new covenant “not like the covenant which I cut with their fathers” (Jer 31:31–32), and Hebrews concludes, “in saying ‘new’ he has made the first old; and what is growing old is near to vanishing” (Heb 8:13). Paul calls the reading of Moses “the old covenant” (2Co 3:14) and the covenant from Sinai one “bearing children for slavery” (Gal 4:24), and says the law, coming 430 years after the promise to Abraham, cannot annul it (Gal 3:17). Hebrews sets the blood of Exo 24:8 beside the blood of Christ, by which the new covenant was made (Heb 9:15, 18–20). From the verses: the covenant at Horeb was a covenant of law resting on Israel's obedience; Israel broke it, and it gave way to the new covenant in Christ's blood; it never replaced the promise to Abraham, which came before it.

Yahweh “cut a covenant with my chosen, swore to David my servant: your seed I will establish for ever, and build your throne to all generations” (Psa 89:4–5). David's last words call it “an everlasting covenant, ordered in all things and kept” (2Sa 23:5). It is sworn and will not be broken: “my covenant I will not profane, nor alter what has gone out of my lips” (Psa 89:35); it is as sure as the covenant with day and night, “that he should not have a son reigning on his throne” (Jer 33:20–21, 25–26). Yet the same psalm laments, “you have renounced the covenant of your servant; you have profaned his crown to the ground” (Psa 89:40), and of the last king of Judah Yahweh said, “remove the crown … it shall be no more, until he comes whose right it is, and I will give it to him” (Ezk 21:31–32). The Branch of David will “reign as king and act wisely, and do justice and righteousness in the land” (Jer 23:5). The angel told Mary that God would give her son “the throne of his father David, and he shall reign over the house of Jacob for ever” (Luk 1:32–33); Peter says David, knowing that God had sworn to set one of his seed on his throne, spoke of the resurrection of the Christ (Act 2:30–31); and Isaiah's “everlasting covenant, the sure mercies of David” is given in Jesus' resurrection (Isa 55:3; Act 13:34). From the verses: the covenant with David promises a son of David reigning on David's throne over Israel for ever; Jesus, raised to die no more, is that son, and the throne, empty since Zedekiah, is his when he comes to reign in the land.

Yahweh promised, “days are coming when I will cut with the house of Israel and the house of Judah a new covenant … I will put my law within them and write it on their heart, and I will be their God and they shall be my people … for I will forgive their iniquity and remember their sin no more” (Jer 31:31–34). Ezekiel calls it “a covenant of peace, an everlasting covenant”, made when Yahweh gathers Israel from the nations into their own land, one nation under one king, “David my servant”, with his sanctuary among them for ever (Ezk 37:21–26). Isaiah's servant is himself given “as a covenant of the people, a light of the nations” (Isa 42:6; 49:8). Jesus said over the cup, “this cup is the new covenant in my blood, which is poured out for you” (Luk 22:20), “for many, for the forgiveness of sins” (Mat 26:28); Hebrews quotes Jer 31:31–34 of the covenant he mediates (Heb 8:6–13) and says he is its mediator “so that, a death having taken place … those who are called may receive the promise of the eternal inheritance” (Heb 9:15). Paul calls the apostles “ministers of a new covenant” (2Co 3:6), and of Israel says, “all Israel shall be saved, as it is written, The deliverer shall come out of Zion … and this is my covenant with them, when I take away their sins” (Rom 11:26–27, from Isa 59:20–21). From the verses: the new covenant was made in the blood of Christ, who mediates it now to all who are called and gives them the promised inheritance; its promise to the house of Israel and the house of Judah will be kept when the deliverer comes out of Zion, gathers Israel into their land and takes away their sins.

Daniel's seventy weeks close with this: after the sixty-two weeks “Messiah shall be cut off, and not for himself”, and the people of a prince to come shall destroy the city and the sanctuary (Dan 9:26); “and he shall make strong (וְהִגְבִּיר) a covenant for the many one week, and in the half of the week he shall cause sacrifice and offering to cease” (Dan 9:27). Jesus named the covenant made for the many at the supper, “my blood of the covenant, poured out for many” (Mat 26:28), the many whose sins the servant bore (Isa 53:11–12); Paul says Christ became a minister of the circumcision “to confirm the promises made to the fathers” (Rom 15:8); and Hebrews says that by his one offering “where there is forgiveness of these, there is no longer an offering for sin” (Heb 10:12, 18). Jesus took up Daniel's abomination of desolation for the end of the temple within his own generation, “when you see Jerusalem surrounded by armies, then know that its desolation has come near” (Mat 24:15, 34; Luk 21:20). From the verses: the one who makes the covenant strong in Dan 9:27 is the Messiah cut off in Dan 9:26, whose death ratified the covenant for the many and ended the worth of sacrifice and offering; the desolation that followed was the destruction of Jerusalem and its temple by the Romans in AD 70.

note: Words: בְּרִית takes b.da.ab; b.dc.ak (בְּרִית, a zero-token cross-reference to אֵל and בַּעַל) is not named. The verb takes b.cz.aa, whose 9 tokens include Dan 4:12, 20 בָּרָא, Biblical Aramaic “the field” (root בר), filed here by spelling and left to that root's entry; Isa 40:26 and Jer 31:22 are ברא and already excluded by the brief. b.da.ad (בָּרוּת) and m.ai.aw (מִבְרָה) are zero-token cross-references, not named; what מִבְרָה refers to was not traced. Lam 4:10 לְבָרוֹת is filed as the piel by the brief's key; MACULA lemmatises it as the noun בָּרוּת, and it may be either. The qal “choose” (1Sa 17:8, בְּרוּ) is kept here by form; the sense may belong with ברר “purify, select”, which has no entry yet. Etymology of בְּרִית is open: the verb “eat” with covenant meals (Gen 26:30; 31:54; Exo 24:11; Jos 9:14), Akkadian birītu “fetter”, and birīt “between” are all recorded only as possible; no cognate is sure, so lexicon-support shows no support for any word. Leads not followed: an Akkadian barû “eat one's fill” (Klein's lead) is not in the Oracc glossary and was not checked in CAD; Arabic بُرَة “nose ring” (Lane p. 197, art. برو) as a “ring, band” behind בְּרִית, too far to record; Jastrow's later Hebrew הַבְרָאָה, the meal served to mourners after a burial (M. Kat. III 7), matches 2Sa 3:35 but is Hebrew, not a cognate. No Ugaritic or Phoenician ברת was checked. The Peshitta renders בְּרִית by ܩܝܡܐ and διαθήκη by ܕܝܬܩܐ, neither of this root.
